new_entities.name: High homocysteine
new_entities.description: Circulating homocysteine concentrations above the usual reference range.

edges.effect_quant: Higher genetically predicted homocysteine was associated with any stroke in Mendelian randomization (OR 1.11 per 1-SD increase, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.21), while meta-analytic observational data show higher coronary and stroke risk at higher homocysteine levels.
edges.mechanism: Homocysteine can plausibly contribute to endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and thrombotic tendency, which is why it has remained a durable cardiovascular biomarker candidate. The unresolved question is whether it acts as a direct driver across the whole CVD spectrum or more selectively in certain vascular endpoints such as stroke.
edges.summary: High homocysteine remains a real cardiovascular warning signal, but the causality story is more specific than older broad claims implied. The observational literature links higher levels to coronary disease and especially stroke, while Mendelian-randomization evidence supports a modest stroke association more clearly than a universal causal effect across all cardiovascular outcomes.
edges.caveats: This edge is intentionally modest because homocysteine may be more important for some vascular phenotypes than others, and lowering homocysteine has not translated into uniformly dramatic CVD prevention. It is better read as a small harmful signal with stronger cerebrovascular support than as a master explanation for all cardiovascular disease.
